question: The International Court of Justice is located at _______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Hague**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **International Court of Justice (ICJ)** is the principal judicial organ of the **United Nations** established in **1945** by the Charter of the United Nations.
 
• The ICJ is located in **The Hague, Netherlands**, which serves as the seat of its operations and is the only principal UN organ based outside New York.
 
• It primarily resolves disputes between **states** and provides advisory opinions on legal questions referred to it by authorized international organizations and UN bodies.
 
• The ICJ is housed in the **Peace Palace**, a historic building in The Hague, which also accommodates other legal institutions.
 
• The Court is composed of **15 judges** elected for nine-year terms by the **United Nations General Assembly** and the **Security Council**. Judges represent various legal systems globally.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Functions of the ICJ:**

 
 
• The ICJ settles disputes submitted by states based on **international law**. These disputes can involve territorial issues, treaty interpretations, and diplomatic relations.
 
• It provides **advisory opinions** on legal questions referred by international bodies, helping clarify international legal principles.
 
• Its rulings are binding for the states involved in the dispute but lack enforcement mechanisms; compliance is based on states' goodwill and international pressure.
 
 
 
• **History and Establishment:**
 
 
• The ICJ was established in **1945** and began its operations in **1946**, succeeding the **Permanent Court of International Justice** of the League of Nations.
 
• The ICJ is governed by its **Statute**, which is an integral part of the UN Charter.
 
• The Peace Palace in The Hague was constructed in **1913** and initially housed the Permanent Court of International Justice.
 
 
 
• **Composition and Selection of Judges:**
 
 
• Judges are elected by the **UN General Assembly** and **Security Council** from a list of candidates nominated by national groups of the Permanent Court of Arbitration.
 
• They represent major legal systems globally and maintain impartiality in their judgments.
 
• The ICJ president and vice-president are elected by the judges themselves for three-year terms.
 
 
 
• **Key Cases:**
 
 
• Some notable cases include the **Corfu Channel Case** (1949), the **Advisory Opinion on Nuclear Weapons** (1996), and the **Whaling in the Antarctic Case** (2014).
 
• These cases have influenced international law, particularly on issues like sovereignty, environmental conservation, and human rights.
 
 
 
• **Other Legal Institutions in The Hague:**
 
 
• The Hague is also home to other international legal bodies, such as the **International Criminal Court (ICC)**, the **Permanent Court of Arbitration (PCA)**, and the **Special Tribunal for Lebanon**.
 
• These institutions contribute to The Hague's status as a global center for international law and justice.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **ICJ vs. ICC:**

 
 
• The ICJ primarily handles disputes between states, while the ICC prosecutes individuals for **war crimes, genocide, crimes against humanity**, and aggression.
 
• Both institutions are located in **The Hague**, but their mandates and functions differ significantly.
 
 
 
• **Jurisdiction:**
 
 
• The ICJ's jurisdiction is based on the consent of states. States can voluntarily submit disputes or accept compulsory jurisdiction through treaties.
 
• It does not have jurisdiction over disputes involving private parties or non-state entities.
 
 
 
• **Membership:**
 
 
• All **193 UN member states** are parties to the ICJ Statute, making its decisions relevant globally.
 
• Non-member states can also access the ICJ for dispute resolution under specific conditions.
 
 
 
• **Significance:**
 
 
• The ICJ plays a crucial role in promoting **peaceful dispute resolution** and reinforcing the rule of law at the international level.
 
• Its advisory opinions contribute to shaping international legal norms and frameworks.
